records.title: Hegseth dodges impeachment after using troops and vets for cover
records.summary: Observers are reporting that absent Democrats likely torpedoed Thomas Massie's attempt to impeach Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth in the House last night. The vote to refer his eight articles of impeachment to the judiciary committee for a sure death, passed 211-204. Hegseth and his compadres in the Pentagon are no doubt feeling vindicated since he spent Tuesday morning boasting of his handling of the war policies in Yemen, the Caribbean, Venezuela, and in particular, Iran. In order to do this he had to engage in some serious fabrications about the state of the war: that it was "won," that Iran's military is "in ruin," the "ironclad blockade (is) unbroken," that "we control the Strait of Hormuz." It is worth watching in full . "For the first time in American history, a cabinet secretary overseeing America's military is being attacked not for losing conflicts with our enemies, but for winning them," Hegseth declared. records.title: 'It's An Invasion': Tiny Spanish Island Of 12,000 Takes In 1,261 Migrants In One Day
records.summary: 'It's An Invasion': Tiny Spanish Island Of 12,000 Takes In 1,261 Migrants In One Day Authored by Etienne Fauchaire via The Epoch Times , EL HIERRO, Spain - Shortly before noon on Sunday, a wooden fishing boat carrying hundreds of African migrants was brought into the small harbor of La Restinga, on the southern tip of the Spanish island of El Hierro. About half an hour later, a second boat arrived with dozens more on board. An hour after that, hundreds more followed. In total, El Hierro received 1,261 migrants aboard seven boats on Sunday alone, topping 1,000 arrivals for the second consecutive day , according to Spanish news agency EFE. The smallest and westernmost of Spain's main Canary Islands, in the Atlantic off northwest Africa, it has about 12,000 residents. So far this year, about 17,000 illegal migrants have landed there, out of roughly 27,000 for the whole archipelago , Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres told reporters on Sunday during a visit to La Restinga. Since Nov. 1, the island has received 96 migrant boats, compared with 66 in the first 10 months of the year , EFE reported. records.title: Van Eyck: The Portraits review – a jewel box of phenomenal death-defeating paintings
records.summary: National Gallery, London Bringing together all the pioneering master’s portraits for the first time reveals the way he clinically preserved monsters, merchants – even his wife – like flies in amber The stubble is tiny yet silver-sharp on the chin of an unknown old man whom Jan van Eyck painted in oils 600 years ago: so long after both are dead you can still see this bloke needs a shave. The hairs on top of his head are just as miraculously caught, varying individually in paleness and lankness. You feast your eyes on the sagging skin of his throat with its overhangs and shady gulleys like a rock formation. He is a wonder, a freak of nature and yet a perfectly ordinary person. So are we all banal and marvellous, mundane and impossible, suggests Van Eyck. The National Gallery has created a jewel box of a show bringing together all Van Eyck’s portraits as we define them – a painting of a person for its own sake. Yet portraitist was a long way from being his only job. Van Eyck painted stupendous religious works, including the Ghent Altarpiece that he collaborated on with his brother Hubert. records.title: The corporate boom in vegan food is dead. Long live real plant-based cooking | Isobel Lewis
records.summary: The fad for plant-based junk food has run its course, but restaurants reflecting the centuries-long history of this cuisine still thrive Have you ever gone to make a restaurant reservation and been met with a Google Maps listing bearing that harbinger of doom: “Permanently closed”? It’s a pretty deflating feeling – and one the UK’s vegan population knows well. Over the past few years, many once-beloved, plant-based establishments have shut up shop or moved away from brick-and-mortar businesses, from The Allotment in Manchester to The Vurger Co, which had restaurants in London and Brighton. Each shuttering galvanises the vegan community into supporting their local spots. But they’re gutting too, and deeply felt by a group who see themselves more as an ethically motivated community than simply clientele. The so-called sorry state of the vegan restaurant scene has been widely reported on (not least by me ). But after working with the food magazine Vittles on its inaugural London vegan guide , I have begun to challenge the “death of vegan dining” narrative that I had found myself perpetuating. records.title: Heysel 85 review – rage-filled denunciation of the incompetence that fuelled a football disaster
records.summary: Teodora Ana Mihai and her passionately committed cast reconstruct the grim sequence of bad judgments that led to 39 fans dying Shame and rage are the keynotes of this immersive, viscerally powerful drama-thriller set amid the macabre tragedy of football’s 1985 European Cup final between Juventus and Liverpool in the crumbling Heysel stadium in Brussels. Crowd disorder before kickoff in a poorly maintained, badly policed venue resulted in the deaths of 39 fans. In this film, the roar of the crowd echoing overhead through the stadium’s claustrophobic tunnels is like the wailing of the damned, while the sport’s officer class flinch and panic as if at a wartime loss. Grimly, the match was allowed to go ahead, despite the fatalities; the authorities believed the game itself would restore order on a bread-and-circuses basis, and that abandoning the match would only cause greater violence and chaos. Heysel 85 is directed and co-written by Romanian-born and Belgian-based film-maker Teodora Ana Mihai; she is a former collaborator of Cristian Mungiu, though maybe the influence here is more Paul Greengrass. records.title: Is this Britain’s most beautiful bus journey? The Welsh service that beats the train hands down
records.summary: A new coach service between Holyhead in the north and Carmarthen in the south offers a thrilling glimpse of west Wales, from mountain peaks to pretty seafronts – and it knocks half an hour off the journey As anyone who has ever tried to catch a train from north to south Wales will know, it’s quite the adventure, and by adventure, I mean chore. You leave Wales, dip into England and then back into Wales to complete the journey. The fastest “Marches” route, which includes stops in Chester, Crewe and Shrewsbury, takes about five and a half hours and costs about £105, depending on your ticket. There are lots of reasons for this: mid-Wales has some challenging topography; the old rail networks, before the Beeching cuts, predominantly bled outwards, transporting slate, coal and steel to distant ports and markets. Last month, all that changed. Just not in the way you probably imagine. Continue reading...

records.title: Will Syria entry into Mecca pact mean clash with the Houthis?
records.summary: Syria appears likely to soon join the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, a collective defense agreement established several months ago by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. This development would constitute a milestone in Damascus’ efforts to reassert itself within the region’s security architecture following Syria’s gruesome civil war. Membership in the pact could enhance the legitimacy and prestige of post-Assad Syria while bolstering its military capabilities and deepening partnerships with influential regional states. Syria could benefit from more intelligence cooperation, military training, and Saudi financial support. All this could complement Damascus’ existing security partnership with Ankara. But it’s not all milk and honey. records.title: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take the decision to go to war seriously?
records.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. Less than 1% of Americans serve in the military. records.title: Three Men & A Photo Op: What To Expect In Shenzhen
records.summary: Three Men & A Photo Op: What To Expect In Shenzhen Authored by Larry C. Johnson via Sonar21 , On Thursday, November 19, in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, Donald Trump will sit down with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping for a three-way conversation . Beijing's Foreign Ministry made it official on Monday, calling it the "China-Russia-United States Summit." The Kremlin had already announced it, and the White House had already bragged about it. It really is a first. No American president has ever sat at the same table with the leaders in Moscow and Beijing. Not FDR, who saw Stalin at Tehran and Yalta and saw China's Chiang Kai-shek separately in Cairo. Not Nixon, who went to Beijing and Moscow on separate trips in 1972. Not Reagan or the Bushes. All three of today's leaders sat through the same G20 group photos in Trump's first term, but never at the same negotiating table. Washington's foreign policy establishment is already muttering about a "new Yalta." So what will actually happen? You don't need a crystal ball. You need a calendar. Trump has now held four in-person summits with these two men since August 2025, and they follow a script so predictable you could set your watch by it.

records.summary: Last week, the Trump administration announced that, beginning January 1, South Africa and Rwanda will stop receiving preferential trade access to the U.S. market through the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). This decision comes down to issues that have little to do with the act itself, nor even really with trade between the United States and these countries. Rather, in both cases, their removal from AGOA serves as an act of retribution from a president unhappy with their governments’ policies on domestic or regional issues. But American interests themselves will suffer, as consumers will be forced to pay higher prices for the same goods. The preferential trade agreement — originally signed into law in 2000 by President Bill Clinton and most recently renewed in September for two additional years — provides duty-free access for over 7,000 goods to the U.S. market for qualifying sub-Saharan countries. records.title: Nvidia Lacks Corporate D&O Insurance Amid Huang Scandal
records.summary: Nvidia Lacks Corporate D&O Insurance Amid Huang Scandal Nvidia does not have directors’ and officers’ (D&O) liability insurance covering the company itself, an unusual omission for a major US-listed corporation that could leave the chipmaker facing substantial legal costs amid the controversy surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang, according to Financial Times . The FT writes that while Nvidia reportedly maintains $900mn in insurance protecting its directors and senior executives from personal liability, the policy does not extend to the company’s own financial exposure. The coverage, arranged through Aon and involving insurers including Beazley, AIG and Chubb, is limited to what the industry calls Side A protection. Most large publicly traded US companies also purchase Side B and Side C insurance, which can reimburse corporate legal expenses and cover certain claims brought directly against the company. Nvidia’s decision to operate without these protections is uncommon, although high premiums can lead some businesses to retain such risks themselves. records.summary: "Highest Risk Will Be This Winter": Regulators From 38 Countries Warn Of Nuclear Accident In Ukraine Nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries warned Monday that the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is rising this winter , and called on Russia to stop striking the power grid that Ukraine's reactors need to keep their fuel cool, according to a joint statement seen by Reuters before its release. The statement comes from three European bodies, HERCA, WENRA and NORA, whose members cover every EU country plus the US, Britain, Canada and Japan. The regulators "express our deep concern about the increasing risks to nuclear safety arising from Russia's war against Ukraine," and said they see "an urgent need for Russia to cease attacks against Ukraine's nuclear facilities" and the energy infrastructure those plants depend on. Without a stable grid supply, Ukraine's nuclear plants find it harder to keep nuclear material cool and avoid a meltdown , the regulators said: the kind of meltdown that made Chernobyl in 1986 the world's worst civil nuclear accident, spreading iodine-131, cesium-134 and cesium-137 across Ukraine, Belarus, Russia and much of northern and central Europe.

records.summary: Nvidia Lacks Corporate D&O Insurance Amid Huang Scandal Nvidia does not have directors’ and officers’ (D&O) liability insurance covering the company itself, an unusual omission for a major US-listed corporation that could leave the chipmaker facing substantial legal costs amid the controversy surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang, according to Financial Times . The FT writes that while Nvidia reportedly maintains $900mn in insurance protecting its directors and senior executives from personal liability, the policy does not extend to the company’s own financial exposure. The coverage, arranged through Aon and involving insurers including Beazley, AIG and Chubb, is limited to what the industry calls Side A protection. Most large publicly traded US companies also purchase Side B and Side C insurance, which can reimburse corporate legal expenses and cover certain claims brought directly against the company. Nvidia’s decision to operate without these protections is uncommon, although high premiums can lead some businesses to retain such risks themselves. records.summary: Ulster Hall, Belfast With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers ‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage. They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever. Continue reading...

records.title: ‘All I could smell was fertiliser’: the best (and worst) supermarket instant coffee, tasted and rated
records.summary: Our coffee snob spills the beans on which granules hint at chocolate and caramel, and which leave a bitter note • Everything you need to make great coffee I’m a coffee snob with my own grinder, but I found the haptic thwack, whack and crack of opening the lid and film on a jar of instant coffee strangely invigorating, and rather nostalgic. When I took a deep sniff, however, disaster: all I could smell was fertiliser! Instant coffee is brewed at scorching temperatures, then either freeze-dried in a vacuum or spray-dried using hot air. This industrial process strips away many of the volatile flavour compounds and bright aromas that make fresh coffee smell so good. This gives it an earthier, muskier and more bitter flavour profile, though, thankfully, with a little alchemy and hot water, those more familiar coffee aromas and flavours returned, with notes of chicory, bitter chocolate and burnt sugar. Almost all of these products have a similar industrial imprint, uniform granules and a one-dimensional flavour profile, so they’re ultimately more a simulation of the real thing. records.summary: Kalshi Quietly Bought A Broker As Democrats Prepare To Pounce Kalshi quietly bought a small broker-dealer in July and plans to launch stock trading within the next two months , the Wall Street Journal reported Monday. The firm, FB Securities, was set up in 2024 and is run by CEO John Rosanelli, according to Finra filings, and some of its employees are staying on with Kalshi. The prediction-markets platform plans to list stocks, exchange-traded funds and similar products as it builds itself into a multiasset exchange. Stocks are the next step in a push beyond yes-or-no event contracts into perpetual futures, the crypto-born derivative that never expires, trades around the clock and lets traders use leverage to magnify gains and losses. After rolling out perps on crypto, precious metals and commodities this year, Kalshi launched single-stock perpetual futures on Nov. 5, covering more than 50 companies including McDonald's, Palantir, SpaceX and Meta. Users traded more than $300 million of them on the first morning, co-founder and COO Luana Lopes Lara said . records.summary: US Closes The "Cloud Loophole": Days After Jensen's Exit, New Rule Puts AI Chip Rentals To China And Five "Diversion" Hubs Under License For four years, Washington has banned shipping America's best AI chips to China. For most of that time, Chinese labs have simply rented them instead. On Monday, the Commerce Department finally moved to shut that door , issuing an interim final rule that limits remote access to advanced AI chips and servers , a move Bloomberg tied directly to the "increased scrutiny over semiconductor exports after an alleged espionage scandal involving Nvidia." The department's own framing: "The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries. " In other words, if you can't export the chip to Beijing, you can't export the compute either. records.summary: Savitri Hensman says financially struggling families and communities will be hit the hardest Alan Milburn has a track record of so-called cost-cutting measures that waste billions of pounds in public money while making health worse. The private finance initiative was an expensive mess , though it did help huge companies and rich people get richer. It is less surprising that he wants more benefits for young sick and disabled people slashed than that the government might go along with this ( Some young disabled people to lose Pip in Milburn plan – but can apply to local fund, 12 November ). Financially struggling families and communities will be hit the hardest. The high number of young people not in education, employment or training is probably largely due to past top-level decisions. Austerity, making life tougher for claimants while favouring multimillionaires, fewer youth clubs, underfunded mental health care, long delays in providing assessments and equipment, and making school and university more stressful have not only caused suffering but also been expensive. records.title: Milburn’s historic report on Britain’s lost generation says one key thing: finally, young lives will really matter | Polly Toynbee
records.summary: The year-long Neets inquiry has yielded a slew of new policies. But what matters is the political and social priority shift designed to change this country This week marks a monumental turning point for young people in Britain: finally they will come first, not last. It will mark an end, we must hope, to a perverse system that casts down the future generation and overrewards the already privileged old. There are 1 million Neets (16- to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training) in the UK, and they are partly George Osborne’s progeny. He targeted the young, tearing down the Connexions youth service , careers guidance, youth clubs, family benefits and further education funding. Michael Gove, with his Gradgrind exam fixation , scythed through music, sports, arts, drama and technology – subjects that kept many engaged with school. Remember the playing fields sold , the leisure centres closed , the mental health services for Covid-scarred children cut back . That created a lost generation, but it’s worse than that: Neets are blamed and scorned for what older generations have done to them. Labour’s intent is to prioritise young people from babyhood. Let that begin here. Polly

records.title: Oil Market Flips To Surplus For First Time Since Iran War: IEA
records.summary: Oil Market Flips To Surplus For First Time Since Iran War: IEA Authored by Evgenia Filimianova via The Epoch Times , The International Energy Agency (IEA) has said the global oil market is showing early signs of rebalancing after a rapid recovery in Gulf oil exports pushed global supply above demand for the first time since the war in Iran began . In its latest monthly report, published on Friday, the agency said that global oil supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day (mb/d) in October to 105.4 mb/d . The climb followed a 3 mb/d increase in September. "The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran," the IEA said. The agency forecast that the market would return to a supply surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, with a larger build expected in 2027 . But the agency warned that fuel markets remain under severe pressure, particularly for diesel, and its member countries are accelerating the release of emergency stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel, to bridge the gap. records.title: Three cheers for Melania Trump-led ceasefire in Ukraine
records.summary: The humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky, Ukraine, mediated by First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV and jointly implemented by Ukraine and Russia, is unprecedented since the start of this war in 2022. Its success and people-centered spirit also stand in conspicuous contrast to the repeated attempts by the Trump administration to end the war, which have all ended in frustrated failure. There has been pragmatic, if intermittent, engagement between Russia and Ukraine virtually since the 2022 Russian invasion, around issues like the exchange of prisoners of war and the bodies of the fallen, or the Black Sea Grain Initiative . But until October 27, 2026, no humanitarian ceasefire along the frontline had ever been successfully implemented; it had never even been attempted. The story of how Oleshky became a step on the path towards peace has twists and turns. The town on the left bank of the Dnieper River was occupied on the first day of the 2022 Russian invasion. Following operational activity, the level of chlorine in the water supply may be boosted temporarily. The amount of chlorine is carefully controlled and monitored at our treatment works and strategic points in the distribution system. Water quality samples are taken following burst mains repairs to ensure that a satisfactory water supply is restored to customers If you need further help or advice, please contact us on 03457 440088 and one of our team will be here to help, 24 hours a day. records.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. records.title: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality
records.summary: The historian Stephen Kotkin of Stanford’s Hoover Institution has penned an important new essay on the phenomenon of “junk history”: reductionist or plainly wrong interpretations of historical events that have little or no basis in empirical reality but are nevertheless “marshaled in policy debates as justification for action, up to launching wars.” The emblematic example, which has recently been used by advocates for the war with Iran, is the failure of British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain to truly ensure “peace in our time” at Munich in 1938. As Kotkin once put it, “It turns out not everything is Munich. It turns out Munich wasn’t even Munich when you get down into the nitty-gritty details.” Another example of junk history is what many otherwise well-informed American observers think they know about Sweden’s conduct during World War II and the Cold War. records.title: Scorned Trump boots Rwanda, South Africa from trade deal
records.summary: Last week, the Trump administration announced that, beginning January 1, South Africa and Rwanda will stop receiving preferential trade access to the U.S. market through the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). This decision comes down to issues that have little to do with the act itself, nor even really with trade between the United States and these countries. Rather, in both cases, their removal from AGOA serves as an act of retribution from a president unhappy with their governments’ policies on domestic or regional issues. But American interests themselves will suffer, as consumers will be forced to pay higher prices for the same goods. The preferential trade agreement — originally signed into law in 2000 by President Bill Clinton and most recently renewed in September for two additional years — provides duty-free access for over 7,000 goods to the U.S. market for qualifying sub-Saharan countries. In exchange for this preferential access, AGOA requires countries to meet a set of vague requirements, including reducing barriers to American exporters, ensuring governance and human rights standards, and not posing a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy interest

methodology.reliability: A official primary source/catalogue; B established newsroom or independent research; C specialist, advocacy or aggregator; D alternative commentary; E unverified social/community; U unclassified. Grade describes source class, not the truth of a specific claim.
methodology.confidence: Claim confidence is left unassessed unless an upstream collector supplies a numeric value. Source grade is not claim confidence.
methodology.corroboration: The six views reuse the existing archive. Similar stories, repeated posts, syndicated copy or multiple outlets quoting one origin are not independent corroboration. A human must inspect provenance.
methodology.geolocation: Location is shown only when supplied by the source or upstream archive. No location is inferred from a headline.
methodology.limits: This is open-source situational awareness, not intelligence agency coverage, an emergency warning service, a live market terminal or a verified threat assessment.
